correctness.rationale: The analytic logarithm of (1-z^2)/(1+z^2) gives the full identity (u_*)_y=-(8/pi)Re(z/(1-z^4)). On every closed centered disk, Re(z/(1-z^4)) is at most r/(1-r^4), with equality uniquely at z=r>0. Therefore the Jacobian is strictly positive inside D_{r_M} and vanishes at r_M. Because Re F_M=x, each fixed-x vertical fiber is mapped by a strictly increasing imaginary-coordinate function, proving global injectivity. Lewy's theorem excludes univalence on every larger centered disk.

value.rationale: F_M is the explicit mechanism that disproves the recent harmonic Landau-radius conjecture. The source leaves open whether its displayed real-axis fold is actually the first loss of local or global injectivity as centered disks expand. The accepted result answers that natural geometric question completely: the Jacobian minimum is exact on every centered disk, no off-axis fold occurs first, and the triangular fibers make the map globally injective until the fold radius. This is a natural complete classification of the counterexample's univalence regime.
